questions.explain: Prose: recursive splitting 400–600 tokens with 10–15% overlap; markdown: header-aware with header path prepended; code: function/class boundaries; tables: header-carrying row groups; PDFs: layout-aware extraction first.
options: One fixed 500-token strategy for everything
Split only on word count
Random chunk sizes
Match strategy to structure: recursive for prose, header-aware for markdown, syntactic units for code, header-carrying rows for tables
questions.q: How should chunking strategy vary by document type?

questions.explain: Batch up to 100+ texts per call, retry with backoff and jitter on 429/5xx (never 400s), pin the exact model version, validate dimensions on receipt, and normalize text before embedding.
options: Large batches, backoff with jitter on 429/5xx (never 400s), pinned model versions, dimension validation, text normalization
One text per API call for accuracy
Retry on all errors including 400s
Skip dimension validation to save time
questions.q: What is the chapter's embedding hygiene checklist?

questions.explain: The document is the atomic unit (MERGE + DELETE + bulk INSERT in one transaction), but embedding API calls must happen before opening the transaction — seconds of API latency inside a transaction holds locks and bloats the log.
options: Put the embedding API calls inside the transaction
One transaction per chunk
Embed first, then a short transaction covering only database writes
Transactions are not needed for ingestion
questions.q: Where do embedding API calls belong relative to the ingest transaction?

questions.explain: A dedicated ingest_log tracks every stage; alert on stage failure rate above 1%, embed p95 latency doubling week-over-week, and queue depth growth — ingestion gaps are silent until critical.
options: Log ingestion in the LLM audit log
A dedicated ingest_log per stage with alerts on failure rate, embed latency trends, and queue depth
No observability is needed for ingestion
Only log successful ingestions
questions.q: How is ingestion pipeline health monitored?

questions.explain: Enforce size/page caps at upload, parse timeouts per document, magic-byte content-type sniffing, and quarantine (don't delete) poison documents in a view with the failure reason for users and support.
options: Let parsers run indefinitely
Delete poison documents silently
Retry poison documents forever
Upload caps, parse timeouts, magic-byte sniffing, and quarantine with failure reasons
questions.q: How does the pipeline handle poison documents?
